summary: Bernhard Kölver was an Indologist who studied at Kiel, Glasgow, Göttingen, Frankfurt, and Cologne. He held posts at Cologne, the Nepal Research Centre, Kiel University (chair, 1974–1993), and Leipzig University (chair, 1993–2001).

Bernie Glassman worked in Buddhist studies. He earned degrees at Polytechnic Institute of Brooklyn and UCLA, and studied under traditional teachers Taizan Maezumi and Koryu Osaka. He founded Zen Center of Los Angeles and Zen Peacemakers.

Berthe Jansen specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Leiden University and the University of Oxford, completing her PhD under Jonathan A. Silk at Leiden. She held posts at Heidelberg University and Leiden University.

Berthold Delbrück was a linguist and Indologist who studied under Pott, Weber, Bopp, Steinthal, and Haym, earning degrees at Halle and Berlin. He held posts at Halle and served as professor at Jena from 1870 to 1913.

Berthold Laufer worked in Sinology, Tibetology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Berlin and Leipzig under Conrady and others. He held posts at AMNH, Columbia University, and the Field Museum of Natural History.

Bettina Bäumer is an Indologist, philosopher, and religious studies scholar. She completed her doctorate at Munich and studied under Swami Lakshman Joo. She held posts at Banaras Hindu University, Vienna, the Alice Boner Institute, and IIAS.

Bettine Birge is a scholar of Sinology, history, and archaeology. She studied under Wm. Theodore de Bary and Masaaki Sugiyama, earning her Ph.D. from Columbia University, and was a visiting scholar at Academia Sinica in 1994.

Betty Heimann worked in Indology and philosophy. She studied at Heidelberg, Göttingen, Bonn, Strasbourg, Kiel, and Halle under Simmel, Sieg, and Hultzsch. She held posts at Kiel, Halle, Hamburg, London, Oxford, and Colombo.
Betty Jean Shefts was a scholar of linguistics, Tibetology, and Indology. She studied under Franklin Edgerton and Geshe Ngawang Nyima.
Bhadra Ratna Bajracharya is a scholar in Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. He served as Dean at Lumbini Buddhist University and Chairman of the Lotus Research Centre.

Bhadriraju Krishnamurti was a linguist and Indologist. He studied under Murray Barnson Emeneau at the University of Pennsylvania (PhD). He held posts at Andhra University, UC Berkeley, Osmania University (professor, 1962–1986), and the University of Hyderabad.

Bhagavan Das was an Indologist and philosopher who graduated with an M.A. from the University of Calcutta. He co-founded Banaras Hindu University and Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith, serving as headmaster of the latter from ~1921 to 1926.
Bhagirath Prasad Tripathi was an Indologist and linguist who held posts at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, including head of the Research Department as attested in 1989.

Bhagwan Dash worked in Indology and Tibetology. He studied at the Institute of Teaching and Research in Ayurveda, Tribhuvan University, and the University of Delhi (PhD, ~1973–1978), and worked as a cataloguer for the Library of Congress.

Bhagwanlal Indraji was an Indologist and historian-archaeologist who received an honorary doctorate from Leiden University in 1884. He was a member of the Royal Asiatic Society and the Asiatic Society of Mumbai, and a Fellow at Mumbai University.

Bhajagovinda Ghosh was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who served as Assistant Director at the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology and an Editorial Board Member of the Bulletin of Tibetology (attested 1994).

Bharat Bhushan Vidyalankar is a linguist and Indologist who studied at Gurukula Kangri Vishwavidyalaya, the University of Delhi, and Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar University. He held positions at the Central Institute of Hindi and Kendriya Hindi Shikshan Mandal.
Bhau Daji was an Indologist and historian-archaeologist who studied at Elphinstone College from ~1840 to 1845 and Grant Medical College from ~1845 to 1851.

Bhikkhu Anālayo is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Peradeniya and Marburg. He held posts at the University of Hamburg, Dharma Drum Institute of Liberal Arts, Sri Lanka International Buddhist Academy, and the Barre Center for Buddhist Studies.

Bhikkhu Bodhi is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Ph.D. from Claremont Graduate University and studied under Nyanaponika Thera. He served as editor at the Buddhist Publication Society (1984–2002) and president of BAUS (2013).
